claim_reviews.conclusion: “Account holder” correctly matches a person officially associated with or owning a bank account registered in their name.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Pemilik rekening” is a valid and natural Indonesian expression for the account owner/holder in banking contexts.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Pemegang akaun” is a standard Malaysian Malay expression for account holder; DBP usage supports the term and “akaun” denotes a bank account.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is appropriate because the proposed national preferences differ lexically, while cross-variety alternatives remain possible. There is no misleading false-friend relationship.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: Available references establish the meanings and usage of the proposed forms but do not provide a comprehensive frequency comparison across Indonesian and Malaysian corpora.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation and false-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both Malay answers accurately express “account holder” in the stated banking sense. Indonesian “pemilik rekening” and Malaysian “pemegang akaun” are natural variety-appropriate forms. The relation “different-common-word” is justified as a learner preference contrast, not an exclusive distinction. No false-friend contrast is present.
